A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Diffusing DeBias research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v4 reports original DDB classification results, synthetic-image analyses and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v5 retains those original results and adds experiments on real-data bias amplifiers, weaker correlations, an alternative BAR benchmark and generation quality.

M1.justification: The conditional diffusion process, synthetic-data-trained Bias Amplifier, filtered pseudo-labeling with G-DRO, and frozen-amplifier loss weighting remain unchanged. The real-data amplifier variants are experimental controls.

E1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds evaluation on an alternative bias-annotated BAR dataset with correlation 0.95. All previous datasets remain. The Waterbirds additions resample the existing dataset and principally extend protocol and robustness testing.

E2.justification: BiaSwap is added to the original BAR and BFFHQ comparisons in Tables 1b and 2a, reporting 52.40 and 58.87 respectively. DisEnt+BE appears alongside ERM and ETF-Debias in the new annotated-BAR comparison. Existing comparator membership is retained.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce Waterbirds resampling at correlations 0.90, 0.80 and 0.70, real-data amplifier controls using one or 50 epochs, reduced diffusion-training budgets, and FID evaluation. Appendix A.7 specifies manual assessment of 1,000 generated images per class per correlation. Existing benchmark settings in Appendices A.2–A.4 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Validation expands substantially beyond the retained image-count, guidance, filtering and unbiased-data analyses. Section 4.3 directly tests synthetic versus real amplifier-training data; Appendix A.5 tests weaker correlations and generation-quality sensitivity; new Appendix A.7 quantifies bias amplification across training correlations. The earlier caption analysis remains as A.8.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three independent runs and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting for the main benchmarks. Both mix point estimates and uncertainty-bearing results elsewhere. v5 introduces no new seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance test.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark and ablation values are unchanged, but substantial new findings are reported. Real-data amplifier controls yield WGAs of 79.43 and 78.45; annotated BAR gives DDB-I 85.36 ± 0.71. Tables 7, 9 and 10 add weaker-correlation accuracies, FID/performance trade-offs and generated bias ratios. These are additional results under specified conditions, not improvements to retained scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem setting, diffusion and guidance equations, pseudo-labeling rule, and loss weighting are retained. Equations 1–3 match exactly after normalizing spacing. The new amplification explanation is qualitative; no theorem, proof or derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: synthetic bias amplification avoids real conflicting-sample memorization, supports two debiasing recipes and achieves strong benchmark performance. v5 supplies additional empirical support without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: v5 adds a high-density-sampling explanation for bias amplification and interprets the quality ablation as evidence that bias cues matter more than photorealism. The limitations now discuss computational savings, the trade-off against manual bias annotation, and the absence of million-scale evaluation.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a code-repository link. New resource information includes approximately 9.5 hours for 170k BFFHQ diffusion iterations and 3.2 hours for Waterbirds at 32 × 32 resolution. Existing architecture, optimizer and recipe hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 explicitly expands discussion of BiaSwap and positions generating functionally biased data as requiring less semantic fidelity than generating bias-conflicting samples. The bibliography contains the same works; the update of Efficient Bias Mitigation Without Privileged Information to its conference citation is bibliographic.

P1.justification: There are localized additions and rewrites in related work, experimental explanations, conclusions and limitations, plus updated affiliations, conference information and acknowledgements. The main narrative structure remains intact; the caption-analysis appendix is renumbered following the new amplification section.

P2.justification: The wide benchmark table becomes four dataset-specific panels, and the UrbanCars table explicitly separates bias-informed comparators. Four compact analysis tables are added, captions move above tables, and some figures relocate. Existing diagrams, image grids and histogram graphics are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The real-data amplifier control and the weaker-bias, generation-quality and amplification analyses strengthen empirical support for the existing rationale. Clearer comparisons and the code link also improve usability. These benefits outweigh limited reporting flaws: Table 8 cites ETF-Debias inconsistently with Table 2a, and the new 32 × 32 efficiency claim lacks an accompanying quantitative accuracy comparison.
